title: Review: Newton's third law; Newton's second law; Newton's law of gravitation and field strength; Friction
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: C03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; C03-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C03-1#N.3, D03-1#N.2, D04-1#N.5, D05-1#N.7b, C03-1#N.12, D03-1#N.7b, D04-1#N.4, D05-1#N.11a, C03-1#N.8b, D03-1#N.9. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Gravitational field strength
items.clue: Force per unit mass on a small test mass, in N kg⁻¹.

items.label: Uniform field
items.clue: Model used near the surface, where g barely changes.

items.label: Weight
items.clue: Pull on a book by Earth; its partner acts upward on Earth by the book.

items.label: Newton's second law
items.clue: Relationship in which a is proportional to F for one mass and to 1/m for one F.

questions.stem: Two objects exert gravitational forces of magnitude F on each other. The mass of each object is doubled, and the distance between their centres is tripled. What is the new magnitude of the gravitational force that each object exerts on the other?

A crate slides to the left across a level floor with negligible friction. At one instant, two students push on it horizontally: one pushes to the left with a force of 20 N, and the other pushes to the right with a force of 30 N. Which statement about the crate at this instant is correct?

options.text: Its speed is increasing, as there is a net force exerted on it.
Its acceleration is to the left, the direction it is moving.
Its speed is decreasing, as its acceleration is to the right.
Its speed is constant, as the net force exerted on it is constant.

questions.stem: A horse pulls a cart along a level road, and both speed up from rest. A student argues: "The cart pulls back on the horse with a force equal in magnitude to the horse's pull on the cart, so these forces cancel and the cart cannot speed up." Which statement correctly identifies the flaw in the argument?

options.text: The two forces act on different objects, so they cannot cancel.
The horse pulls harder than the cart pulls back while they speed up.
The cart pulls back after the horse's pull has set it moving.
A cart cannot pull on anything, so no force acts back on the horse.

questions.stem: A 0.80 kg box rests on a level floor. The coefficients of friction between the box and the floor are μ_s = 0.60 and μ_k = 0.35. A student pushes the box horizontally, increasing the push slowly from zero. Use g = 10 m/s². What is the magnitude of the push when the box starts to slide?

Planets A and B are uniform spheres with the same density. Planet A has radius R and planet B has radius 2R. Identical probes are placed in shafts inside the planets, each at a distance R/2 from its planet's center. F_A and F_B are the magnitudes of the gravitational forces exerted on the probes by their planets. Which is correct?

Block P of mass m and block Q of mass 2m are connected by an ideal string and rest on a level surface with negligible friction. A student pulls block P with a constant horizontal force of magnitude F, directed away from Q, and both blocks speed up together. What is the tension in the string?
A lamp hangs at rest from a cord fixed to the ceiling. The cord exerts an upward force on the lamp. Which force forms a Newton's third law pair with this force?

options.text: The gravitational force exerted on the lamp by Earth
The downward force exerted on the cord by the lamp
The upward force exerted on the cord by the ceiling
The gravitational force exerted on Earth by the lamp

questions.explanation: The cord pulls up on the lamp, so the lamp pulls down on the cord: the same contact interaction, equal in size, opposite in direction, on the other object.

questions.stem: A book lies on the flat bed of a pickup truck. The truck speeds up from rest along a straight, level road, and the book does not slide on the bed. Which statement about friction on the book is correct?

options.text: Friction pushes the book backward, opposite to its motion.
No friction acts, since the book does not slide on the bed.
Kinetic friction from the bed pushes the book forward, as the book moves along the road.
Static friction from the bed pushes the book forward.

questions.stem: An astronaut's weight at Earth's surface is W. Planet Q has three times Earth's mass and twice Earth's radius. What is the astronaut's weight at the surface of planet Q?

A student stands on a scale in an elevator in three situations. 1: the elevator moves upward at constant speed. 2: the elevator moves upward and is slowing down. 3: the elevator moves downward and is slowing down. The acceleration has the same magnitude in situations 2 and 3. The scale readings are R1, R2 and R3. Which ranking is correct?
